claim: The Legislature convenes on the second Tuesday of January
quote: on the second Tuesday of January at 12 o'clock m.

claim: A regular session is held every year and lasts at most forty legislative days
quote: A regular session of the Legislature shall be held each year and shall not exceed forty legislative

claim: During session the governor has five days (not counting weekends and holidays) to act on a bill
quote: within five days, not including Saturdays, Sundays, or holidays, of presentation

claim: After the Legislature adjourns sine die or recesses for more than five days, the governor has fifteen days to act
quote: within fifteen days after such adjournment or start

claim: No act takes effect until ninety days after adjournment unless passed as an emergency
quote: No act shall take effect until ninety days

claim: Acts of a regular session take effect on 1 July unless they say otherwise
quote: takes effect on the first day of July after its passage

claim: The primary is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June of even-numbered years
quote: on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June of every even-numbered year

claim: The general election is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even-numbered years, and county officers are elected at it
quote: the several state, district, and county officers

claim: Any local governing body may choose to hold its election with the June primary, with county approval
quote: may choose to hold their elections in conjunction with the regular June primary election

claim: Municipalities hold an election every year, in June or November, and the governing body sets which by January 14
quote: each municipality must hold an election of officers each year on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June or the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November

claim: The municipal governing body sets the election date by January 14 of the election year
quote: The governing body shall establish the date of the regular election by January fourteenth of the election year.

claim: A municipality may by ordinance hold its regular election only in even-numbered years
quote: may, by ordinance, choose to hold the regular municipal election only in even-numbered years

claim: In even-numbered years the municipal election is held with the June primary or the November general election
quote: in even-numbered years, hold the general municipal election in conjunction with the regular June primary election or the regular November general election

claim: In odd-numbered years a municipality may hold its election jointly with the school district
quote: may, in odd-numbered years, choose to hold a general municipal election in conjunction with a regular school district election

claim: No municipal election is held where every race is uncontested and there is no ballot question
quote: The number of nominating petitions filed for each vacant position to be filled does not exceed the number of vacancies

claim: Municipal candidates appear on the ballot with no designation other than the office
quote: shall be arranged without any other designation than that of the office for which they are candidates

claim: Municipal candidates are nominated by petition, and filing it constitutes nomination
quote: Upon verification, the filing of a nominating petition constitutes nomination.

claim: Municipal races are won by plurality unless an ordinance passed at least six months earlier requires a runoff
quote: the person having the highest number of votes for any municipal office is elected

claim: A municipality may require runoffs by ordinance at least six months before the election
quote: by ordinance enacted at least six months before the election, require a runoff election

claim: Where a runoff ordinance exists, a runoff is held three weeks later if no one in a race of three or more wins a majority
quote: a runoff election shall be held three weeks from the date of the first election

claim: School districts hold an annual election in June or November, chosen by board resolution
quote: each school district must hold an annual election on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in June or the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November

claim: In even-numbered years the school board election is held with the June primary or the November general election
quote: in even-numbered years, hold the school board election in conjunction with the regular June primary election or the regular November general election

claim: No party affiliation appears on a school ballot
quote: No party affiliation may appear on the ballot

claim: School board candidates are nominated by petition
quote: the filing of the nominating petition constitutes nomination

claim: School boards have five, seven or nine members on three-year terms, which the board may change to two or four years for joint elections
quote: A school board consists of five, seven, or nine members whose terms are from one to three years initially, and three years thereafter

claim: A school board may change terms to four or two years to hold joint elections
quote: increase the length of terms from three to four years or decrease the length of terms from three to two years

claim: Conservation district supervisors are nominated by petition and elected on a nonpolitical ballot at the general election
quote: The auditor shall prepare ballots substantially in the form of the nonpolitical ballot

claim: Ranked choice voting is banned, including by charter or ordinance
quote: a political subdivision may not adopt or enforce in any manner a rule, resolution, charter provision, or ordinance

claim: Only registered members of a party may vote that party's primary ballot
quote: No person may vote a party ballot at any primary election unless the person is registered as a member of that political party

claim: A party may open its primary to voters registered with no party affiliation
quote: may allow for participation in the party's primary elections by any person who is registered to vote with no party affiliation

claim: A party candidate must be registered with that party
quote: unless that person is a registered voter with that party affiliation

claim: A primary is won by the most votes
quote: who receives the highest number of votes cast by the voters of his party

claim: Primary runoffs apply only to U.S. Senate, U.S. House and Governor, below 35 percent
quote: If no candidate for United States Senate, United States House of Representatives, or Governor in a race involving three or more candidates receives thirty-five percent

claim: Sheriff, auditor, register of deeds, treasurer, state's attorney and coroner are nominated and elected on political ballots
quote: on political ballots shall apply to the nomination and election of a sheriff, county auditor, register of deeds, treasurer, state's attorney, and coroner

claim: County commissioner candidates file partisan petitions (and independents their own)
quote: for county commissioner district candidates

claim: An independent is nominated by certificate of nomination signed by registered voters of the district
quote: who is not nominated by a primary election may be nominated by filing a certificate of nomination

claim: A primary candidate may not file as an independent for the same office in the same year
quote: for an office for which he has been a candidate in the primary election of the same year

claim: Voters may not sign a party candidate's petition for a party they are not in, and may not sign for more candidates than seats
quote: For a political candidate of a party of which the person is not a member

claim: Party members may sign an independent's petition if they have not already signed one for that office
quote: from signing either a petition nominating an independent or a nonpolitical candidate for office if the person has not previously signed a petition for that office to be filled

claim: An independent candidate may be any registered voter regardless of party who declares as independent
quote: any registered voter regardless of party affiliation who declares to be an independent candidate for public office

claim: Each organized county has a board of three to seven commissioners on four-year terms elected at the general election
quote: shall have a board of commissioners consisting of not less than three nor more than seven members

claim: Commissioner seats are staggered by district number between presidential and gubernatorial years
quote: numbered or unnumbered district shall run for election at the general election at which the Governor is elected

claim: Commissioners are nominated and elected by the voters of their district
quote: The nomination and election of county commissioners shall be by a vote of the voters of the district

claim: Voters may change the commission to three, five or seven by petition and election
quote: may be increased to five or seven or reduced to five or three

claim: Counties elect a sheriff, auditor and register of deeds in one cycle, and a treasurer, state's attorney and coroner in the other, on four-year terms, unless a charter says otherwise
quote: Unless otherwise provided by county charter

claim: Counties elect a treasurer, state's attorney and coroner
quote: a treasurer, state's attorney, and coroner

claim: A county commission may combine two or more county offices into one elected office
quote: combine two or more county offices and that one person shall be elected to, and perform the duties of, the combined offices

claim: Counties may adopt an appointed county manager form, with the commission still elected
quote: The board shall be elected in the same manner as provided by chapter

claim: Any county or city may adopt a home rule charter
quote: Any county or city or combinations thereof may provide for the adoption

claim: A charter may set any structure, superior to statute, as long as the legislative body is popularly elected
quote: provided that the legislative body so established be chosen by popular election

claim: A township organized before cannot be abolished without a vote of its voters
quote: No township heretofore organized

claim: Home rule units may not set standards lower than state law
quote: Neither charter nor ordinances adopted thereunder may set standards and requirements which are lower or less stringent than those imposed by state law

claim: Civil township voters hold an annual township meeting on the first Tuesday of March
quote: shall annually assemble and hold a township meeting on the first Tuesday of March

claim: One supervisor is elected each year at the annual meeting for a three-year term
quote: one supervisor, who shall hold his office for the term of three years

claim: A clerk and treasurer are elected at each annual meeting, and a constable may be
quote: At each annual meeting, a clerk and a treasurer shall be elected, and a constable may be elected.

claim: Township officers are elected by ballot unless unopposed
quote: shall be elected by ballot except if there is no opposing candidate

claim: A township may require nominating petitions by ordinance
quote: may, by ordinance, require a candidate for township office to file a nominating petition

claim: Township organization can be abolished by petition and election
quote: abolition

claim: Three classes of municipality by population: first class 5,000 and over, second class 500 to 4,999, third class under 500
quote: Municipalities of the third class: municipal corporations with a population of fewer than five hundred.

claim: A municipality is a city or town
quote: "Municipal corporation" or "municipality," any city or town that is organized pursuant to this title

claim: A municipality whose census population crosses a class line may apply to court to change class
quote: the municipality may, through its governing body, apply to the circuit court having jurisdiction for a judgment authorizing the classification change

claim: Existing classification continues until changed
quote: The present classification of government of existing municipalities continues until changed as provided by this title.

claim: First and second class municipalities have a mayor and council or a commission, with or without a manager; third class have a board of trustees
quote: Each third class municipality must be governed by a board of trustees, with or without a city manager.

claim: First and second class forms
quote: must be governed by a mayor and common council, a mayor and a common council with a city manager, a board of commissioners, or a board of commissioners with a city manager

claim: Existing forms continue until changed
quote: The present form of government of existing municipalities must continue until changed as provided by this title.

claim: Aldermanic mayor term two to five years by ordinance
quote: The mayor holds office for a term of not less than two nor more than five years as determined by ordinance.

claim: Council of mayor plus two aldermen per ward, two-year terms unless ordinance sets three to five
quote: two aldermen elected from and by the voters of each ward

claim: Alderman term default two years, ordinance may set three to five
quote: The term of office for each alderman is two years, unless a municipality adopts an ordinance establishing the term of office to be three, four, or five years.

claim: Second and third class voters may choose at-large aldermen
quote: may, by majority vote, choose to elect aldermen to the common council at large

claim: Commission form: mayor plus two or four commissioners at large
quote: the board of commissioners shall consist of the mayor and two or four commissioners elected at large

claim: Commission terms two to five years by ordinance
quote: The term of office of the mayor and commissioners is not less than two or more than five years, as determined by ordinance

claim: Commission with manager: nine at-large commissioners
quote: the number of at-large commissioners is nine

claim: Board of trustees has three or five members at large
quote: The board of trustees of a municipality consists of either three or five members elected at large.

claim: Trustees serve three-year terms
quote: A member of the board of trustees holds office for a term of three years

claim: Voters can change form of government or number of wards, commissioners or trustees by petition and election
quote: upon a question of the number of wards, commissioners, or trustees

claim: Statute addresses home rule election costs for counties and first and second class municipalities
quote: counties, and first and second class municipalities are authorized to expend from their general funds

claim: Title 12 applies to township, municipal, school and other local elections unless their own statutes say otherwise
quote: The provisions of this title apply to township, municipal, school, and other subdivision elections unless otherwise provided

claim: School districts hold no election when every race is uncontested and there is no question
quote: does not exceed the number of vacancies

claim: The school board picks the election date by resolution early in the year
quote: The school board shall select the date of the election by resolution no later than the first regular meeting after January first of each year.

claim: A school board term change is subject to referendum on petition
quote: is subject to a referendum if five percent of the registered voters of the school district

claim: Civil township organization happens on petition of the voters, so some areas are unorganized
quote: shall petition the board of county commissioners for civil township organization
